tasks.description: Implement multivariate linear regression in PyTorch using Huber loss on a synthetic dataset with injected outliers.

requirements.math: Define Huber loss and explain why it is more robust than MSE in the presence of outliers.
requirements.data: Synthetic multivariate regression dataset with 5 features and 10 percent target outliers.
requirements.implementation: Use torch.nn.Linear and manual training loop with torch.optim.Adam.
requirements.evaluation: The evaluate() function must compute MSE, R2, and MAE on the VALIDATION split.
requirements.validation: Assert validation R2 > 0.75 and that Huber loss performs better than plain MSE baseline on MAE.
requirements.output: Return dict with loss history, validation metrics, and baseline comparison.

tasks.algorithm: Linear Regression (Batch vs Mini-batch Gradient Descent)
tasks.description: Compare full-batch and mini-batch training for linear regression on synthetic multivariate data.

requirements.math: Explain gradient descent update rule and the difference between batch and mini-batch optimization.
requirements.data: Synthetic regression dataset with 8 features and moderate Gaussian noise.
requirements.implementation: Train the same torch.nn.Linear model twice: once with full-batch updates and once with mini-batch DataLoader updates.
requirements.evaluation: The evaluate() function must compute MSE and R2 on the VALIDATION split for both models.
requirements.validation: Assert both models achieve validation R2 > 0.85 and compare convergence histories.
requirements.output: Return dict with both training histories and final metric comparison.

tasks.algorithm: Logistic Regression (Binary Classification on Breast Cancer Dataset)
tasks.description: Implement binary logistic regression in PyTorch on sklearn breast cancer data with feature standardization.

requirements.math: Include sigmoid function and binary cross-entropy loss in LaTeX.
requirements.data: Use sklearn.datasets.load_breast_cancer with train validation split.
requirements.preprocessing: Standardize features using training set statistics only.
requirements.implementation: Use torch.nn.Linear with BCEWithLogitsLoss and Adam optimizer.
requirements.evaluation: The evaluate() function must compute loss, accuracy, precision, recall, F1, and ROC-AUC on the VALIDATION split.
requirements.output: Return dict with loss history and final classification metrics.

tasks.algorithm: Logistic Regression (L1 Regularization for Sparse Features)
tasks.description: Implement binary logistic regression with L1 regularization in PyTorch and inspect feature sparsity.

requirements.math: Define binary cross-entropy with an added L1 penalty term.
requirements.data: Synthetic binary classification dataset with 20 features where only a subset are informative.
requirements.implementation: Use torch.nn.Linear and add L1 penalty manually to the loss inside the training loop.
requirements.evaluation: The evaluate() function must compute accuracy, precision, recall, F1, and sparsity ratio on the VALIDATION split.
requirements.validation: Assert validation accuracy > 0.88 and that at least 30 percent of learned weights are near zero.
requirements.output: Return dict with classification metrics, sparsity statistics, and loss history.
